sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: Dutch-flagged polar vessel arriving Granadilla cargo port, Tenerife, early hours 10 May. Will NOT pier-dock — passengers transferred by inflatable boats to isolated cordoned quayside, then guarded buses to airport, departing by nationality. Disembarkation only begins once repatriation flights confirmed ready at runway. German woman's body remains aboard. Oceanwide confirmed as of 08 May all remaining 147 aboard are asymptomatic and PCR-negative. Weather window closes Tuesday; Canary Islands govt requests ship proceed to Netherlands for decontamination post-disembarkation.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Confirmed source investigation zone. Argentine Health Ministry published 06 May report: Dutch index couple (Cases 1 & 2) conducted 4-month birdwatching road trip (27 Nov 2025–01 Apr 2026) spanning Chile, Uruguay, and Argentina; index case returned from Uruguay only 4 days before departure. Malbrán Institute now actively capturing and testing rodents along the Dutch couple's travel route. WHO working hypothesis: index case infected during activities in Argentina/Chile. No cruise-linked domestic cases confirmed; no Ushuaia hantavirus cases in recent decades. Argentine national tally: 101 infections since Jun 2025.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr (includes Dutch index male body and Dutch widow who later died in Johannesburg). Swiss confirmed male case also disembarked here. UKHSA contact-tracing 82 passengers + 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight ongoing. Disembarkees from 12 countries departed before hantavirus was confirmed (02 May). 7 UK nationals from St Helena disembarkation traced by UKHSA; 2 self-isolating in UK.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, 69, PCR+) died at Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — sole WHO-confirmed Andes virus death as of 08 May. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; condition improved and transferred to Netherlands. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight (82 pax + 6 crew). Asymptomatic South African woman (briefly in Barcelona) confirmed located and monitored in South Africa.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee, 56) transferred to Netherlands after condition improved. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed postmortem that German woman died of Andes virus. KLM flight attendant admitted Amsterdam UMC 07 May with mild symptoms — tested NEGATIVE 08 May; not a secondary transmission case. RIVM: 2 of 3 symptomatic KL592 contacts tested negative; 1 result pending. GGD continuing contact tracing of KL592 passengers. Four medical staff remain aboard Hondius.

sites.name: LONDON
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed 2 British nationals PCR+ (one transferred to Netherlands, one treated South Africa) and flagged a 3rd suspected case on Tristan da Cunha (08 May). UK repatriation flight arranged for 19 passengers and 4 crew from Tenerife; FCDO/UKHSA RDT pre-positioned. Returning asymptomatic Britons to isolate up to 45 days per UKHSA guidance. US and UK both confirmed repatriation flights to Tenerife.

sites.name: PARIS
sites.desc: Eight French nationals identified as close contacts of confirmed case on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight — none were on the cruise. One reporting mild symptoms, isolated pending PCR results. French health ministry coordinating diagnostics and quarantine measures.

sites.name: ZURICH
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger (one of 30 who disembarked St Helena 24 Apr) self-presented after symptom onset; confirmed Andes virus at University Hospital Zurich — confirmed 06 May. Wife (also on trip) asymptomatic and isolating. Swiss authorities conducting additional contact tracing for anyone who came into contact with the patient after he returned to Switzerland.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, developed pneumonia). Netherlands laboratory postmortem PCR returned Andes virus positive; WHO notes cause of death still officially under investigation as of 08 May. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact evacuated 06 May to Netherlands, subsequently returned to Germany (Düsseldorf) for monitoring. RKI contact tracing active.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: 32-year-old woman hospitalized in negative-pressure isolation with respiratory symptoms consistent with hantavirus; was a passenger on same 25 Apr St Helena–Johannesburg flight as deceased Dutch woman. Health Secretary Padilla noted this is 'a pretty unlikely case' given seating distance. PCR results pending as of 09 May. Valencia Regional Health coordinating.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius arriving Granadilla cargo port early 10 May — will NOT pier-dock. Passengers evacuated in inflatable boats to isolated cordoned quayside; guarded buses via TF1 route to airport (~15 min). Disembarkation only begins once repatriation aircraft confirmed ready at runway. Weather window closes Tuesday. WHO/CDC/UKHSA/ECDC/RIVM teams pre-positioned. Canary Islands govt requests ship sail to Netherlands for decontamination post-disembarkation.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Gómez Ulla Military Hospital fully activated to receive 14 Spanish Hondius passengers. PCR on arrival + Day 7; twice-daily temperature checks; single rooms, no visitors. Protocol covers all aboard between 01 Apr–10 May or in close contact with confirmed case. Biosecurity equivalent to Ebola/COVID-19 protocols; 60–80 additional staff recruited. High-Level Isolation Unit (UAAN, 22nd floor) on standby.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent approximately one week in Barcelona before returning to South Africa. Located and confirmed asymptomatic. No local transmission identified.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed suspected hantavirus case (08 May): British male passenger who likely disembarked Hondius during 13–15 Apr stop; developed symptoms and sought medical advice. Spouse isolating as precaution. 6 additional guests joined Hondius at Tristan da Cunha per Oceanwide, expanding contact tracing scope. Patient currently on island; UKHSA assessing remotely. Island population approximately 220 permanent residents.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: Two male residents (aged 67 and 65) isolated in government facility; both disembarked Hondius at St Helena and were on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight with confirmed case. One has mild rhinorrhea, second asymptomatic. PCR results pending. CDA notified 04–05 May; public risk in Singapore assessed as low. Both residents arrived Singapore by 04 May.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early. Four Canadians total remain aboard vessel awaiting Tenerife evacuation. PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 09 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH coordinating with local health officials to monitor one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident remains aboard ship and will transit Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC-escorted State Dept charter. No California residents reported ill or infected as of 09 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Georgia DPH monitoring two residents who returned from Hondius. Both in good health with no signs of infection as of 08 May per GDPH statement. Following CDC recommendations. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states; none of the monitored US residents exhibiting signs of illness as of 09 May.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3 (lowest emergency activation tier); Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts per CDC/ABC 08–09 May reporting.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ health authorities monitoring two individuals with potential post-disembarkation exposure to a Hondius passenger. Neither symptomatic as of 09 May. Part of the broader US monitoring cohort per CNN 08 May reporting.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) fully staffed and activated. CDC team pre-deployed to Offutt AFB, Bellevue. 17 American Hondius passengers (including one Utah resident) to arrive via CDC-escorted State Dept biocontainment charter from Tenerife after Sunday docking. NQU medical director Dr. Wadman confirmed all 17 are asymptomatic; anyone developing symptoms to be moved to Biocontainment Unit.

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed 08 May that at least one Utah resident is among the 17 Americans still aboard MV Hondius. Person is asymptomatic and will disembark in Tenerife, then travel with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for quarantine. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 09 May.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none are currently ill as of 08 May. In close coordination with vessel operator and international authorities. Monitoring continues pending Tenerife disembarkation and subsequent repatriation.

sites.name: DUBLIN
sites.desc: Two Irish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per RTE. Ireland is among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board per ECDC briefing. Irish Dept of Health coordinating with ECDC and WHO; returning Irish nationals to quarantine per national protocol.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored off Praia 03–06 May; departed 19:15 local 06 May for Tenerife. Three medevac patients evacuated here 06 May — two flew to Amsterdam (received by specialist teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled refueling stop at Gran Canaria after Morocco refused permission and a medical equipment malfunction caused further delays. Cape Verde assessed unable to handle full passenger evacuation — basis for WHO requesting Tenerife docking. 2,500 Argentine diagnostic kits dispatched to five countries.
